summary.value: HVAC is licensed in North Carolina as 'heating', in three groups, by the same board that licenses plumbing. There is no separate HVAC board.
summary.source_title: Applicant Information — NC Board of Examiners of Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Contractors
summary.evidence: the Plumbing, Heating Group No. 1, Heating Group No. 2 and/or Heating Group No. 3 Contractor examination

jurisdiction_model.local_layer_note: Note the cross-board overlap: North Carolina's ELECTRICAL board issues a Special Restricted 'Plumbing, Heating and Air Conditioning' licence (SP-PH) for the electrical work inside that scope. A North Carolina HVAC company can therefore need a licence from each of two boards.

boards.name: North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Contractors
boards.scope: Plumbing, Heating Groups 1-3, fuel piping and fire sprinkler contractor and technician licences — 31 licence qualifications in total

who_must_hold.value: A contractor installing, maintaining, servicing or repairing heating systems in the Group 1 category.
who_must_hold.source_title: Applicant Information — NC Board of Examiners of Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Contractors
who_must_hold.evidence: an applicant must have 2 years (4,000 hours) on-site full-time experience

required.source_title: Applicant Information — NC Board of Examiners of Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Contractors
required.evidence: All persons desiring to obtain licensure with this Board must meet the requirements listed herein and satisfactorily complete the applicable examination(s).

fee.source_title: FAQ — NC Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Board
fee.evidence: The examination application fee is $150.00 and is non-refundable.

exam.note: The exam must be taken within 90 days of the eligibility notice; a failing candidate waits 90 days before retesting; a passing candidate has 45 days to file the License Activation Form or must retest. Three separate clocks, all of them alertable.

requirement.value: 2 years (4,000 hours) of on-site full-time experience in the installation, maintenance, service or repair of plumbing or heating systems in the category sought, whether or not a licence was required for the work.
requirement.source_title: Applicant Information — NC Board of Examiners of Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Contractors
requirement.evidence: an applicant must have 2 years (4,000 hours) on-site full-time experience

alternatives.value: Up to one-half (2,000 hours, or 45 quarter / 30 semester hours) may be academic or technical training in the same field. Military experience counts with a DD214 and supervisor statements. Code-enforcement experience does NOT count.
alternatives.source_title: Applicant Information — NC Board of Examiners of Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Contractors
alternatives.evidence: Certified Code Enforcement Official experience does not meet the experience requirements for licensure.

application_fee.source_title: FAQ — NC Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Board
application_fee.note: This is the examination application fee. The separate licence activation fee is not published on the board's site.

cycle.source_title: N.C. G.S. 87-22 License fee; expiration and renewal; reinstatement
cycle.evidence: All licenses shall expire on the last day of December in each year following their issuance or renewal.

fee.note: G.S. 87-22 sets a CEILING of $150 for the annual plumbing or heating licence fee, not the fee itself, and the board publishes the actual amount only on the renewal invoice it mails each September. A ceiling is not a price and is not recorded as one.

expiry_rule.source_title: License Renewal — NC Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Board
expiry_rule.evidence: All licenses expire on the last day of December in each year following their issuance or renewal.
expiry_rule.note: Every licence in the state expires on the same day. For a contractor with 30 North Carolina licences that is not 30 deadlines, it is one December wall — which changes what a good alert looks like: a single batch task in October, not thirty reminders.

grace_period.source_title: License Renewal — NC Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Board
grace_period.evidence: Contrary to popular belief, there is NO GRACE PERIOD following the expiration of a license
grace_period.note: An explicit zero, stated by the board in capitals, and all licensed activity (bidding, contracting, supervising, installing) must cease on 1 January until renewal.

late_fee.source_title: N.C. G.S. 87-22 License fee; expiration and renewal; reinstatement
late_fee.evidence: the Board shall increase the license fee by twenty
late_fee.note: Applies on failure to renew during January. A licence unrenewed for three years requires re-examination.

required.source_title: Education — NC Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Board
required.evidence: Mandatory Continuing Education was eliminated by the Board in 2012, and is no longer required in order to renew licenses annually

hours.source_title: Education — NC Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Board
hours.evidence: Mandatory Continuing Education was eliminated by the Board in 2012
hours.note: A positive finding, not a gap. Two North Carolina boards, opposite rules: the plumbing/heating board requires none, the electrical board requires eight hours a year with half in a classroom. A single 'North Carolina CE' rule in a customer's spreadsheet is wrong for one of the two trades.

approved_provider_rule.value: None: the Board does not approve providers or courses and no hours are reported to it.
approved_provider_rule.source_title: Education — NC Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Board
approved_provider_rule.evidence: The Board does not approve providers or courses and there is no need to report CE hours to the Board.

general_liability.note: No liability-insurance minimum appears on the board pages read. G.S. ch. 87 art. 2 was read only at s. 87-22 (fees and renewal); the rest of the article is in the wave-2 queue.

reciprocity_statement.value: None. The board states in terms that it has no reciprocity agreement with any state. Two narrower routes exist: a Technical Examination Waiver Agreement with South Carolina, under which the NC business law exam must still be passed; and the Neighbor State License Recognition Act for people who are permanent NC residents AND hold a licence in Georgia, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia or West Virginia.
reciprocity_statement.source_title: Applicant Information — NC Board of Examiners of Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Contractors
reciprocity_statement.evidence: There are no license reciprocity agreements with any other state.
reciprocity_statement.note: Note the residency condition on the Neighbor State route: it is a rule about the PERSON, not about the company. A Virginia-licensed qualifier who does not move to North Carolina cannot use it.

qualifying_individual_rule.note: The board's licence structure distinguishes licensees from sub-licensees (there is an address-change form for both), but the qualifying-individual rule for a company was not established from the pages read.

per_location_rule.note: Not stated on the pages read.

change_notification_deadline.note: Not stated on the pages read.

typical_timeline.value: Renewals are processed within 2-3 business days of receipt, with 3-5 further days for the printed licence to arrive.
typical_timeline.source_title: License Renewal — NC Plumbing, Heating and Fire Sprinkler Board
typical_timeline.evidence: Renewals are currently being processed within 2-3 business days of receipt
typical_timeline.note: This is the RENEWAL turnaround, the only duration the board publishes. It is not the new-licence timeline, and the playbook must not present it as one.

coverage_notes: The board offers 31 licence qualifications. Two heating contractor groups are modelled; Group 2, the Class I/II technician licences, the state-and-local-government and private-educational technician licences and fuel piping are not.

Heating Group definitions (what distinguishes Group 1 from 2 from 3) are behind the board's 'Contractor License Definitions' link, which was not fetched. The playbook must not tell a customer which group they need.
